text:
maria.g: Heads-up — ran a focused probe on Ember-18B int4 overnight. overall token cost ~50% down vs fp16 on our workloads, but we have a concentrated hit on multi-turn summarization + rerank chains. short write-up in the drive.
aj: brief summary here pls? which workflows regress the most?
maria.g: TL;DR: reranker stacks (3-stage) and long multi-turn summaries (>8 turns or >2000 tokens) show degradation: nDCG down ~6 pts on rerank test, ROUGE-L down ~8 on long summaries. single-turn summarization + short reranks are within noise. latency is acceptable — int4 reduces p95 by ~12ms.
neil: any pattern by activation distribution or specific attention layers? sometimes early-layer quant error propagates.
maria.g: good question. layer-wise error maps show larger L2 drift in layers 20-24 (middle), especially in keys/values. hypothesis: scale variance in KV matmul with our current per-tensor qconfig.
eil: did you try per-channel or per-row scaling?
maria.g: ran two configs: per-tensor symmetric (baseline int4 build) and per-channel asymmetric for KV-heavy ops. per-channel asymmetric improved rerank nDCG by ~3 pts but still ~3 pts below fp16. config snippet pasted below.

```
qcfg_a = {"mode":"int4", "method":"per-tensor", "symmetric":true}
qcfg_b = {"mode":"int4", "method":"per-channel", "symmetric":false, "channels":128}
```

katie.p: product question — are these regressions visible in end-user metrics or just bench slices?
maria.g: Mostly bench slices so far. We did a small holdout A/B on 2% production traffic for rerank-heavy queries and saw a tiny uptick in manual complaint flags (~+0.4%) and a few low-quality re-ranks flagged by the QA team. Not a showstopper but above our tolerance for core search customers.
neil: routing idea: fallback for rerank pipelines and high-turn dialogs to int8/fp16; route short chat + frontend autocomplete to int4. Mixed-fleet.
aj: agree. can we do smarter routing than token count? maybe estimate "rerank-depth" from request metadata.
katie.p: product can add a header flag for rerank pipelines (most do), but some customers use opaque bundles. we need a heuristic fallback: if request.path contains /rerank or payload.rerank_steps > 1 -> durable flag.
eil: ops checklist: shadow-run int4 outputs for rerank paths for 2 weeks, collect nDCG + click-through delta, enable per-query diff logging. also add human-review queue for top 200 mismatch samples.
maria.g: econ note: modeled end-state where we route 70% of traffic to int4 (excluding reranks/longform). net cost reduction ~38% org-wide. conservative mixed-fleet (exclude reranks + >2048 tokens) yields ~21% savings.
aj: what's the suggested canary % and monitoring windows?
maria.g: recommended canary: 3% for 72 hours with automated eval every 6 hours; longform shadowing for 14 days because regressions surface late. rollback if rerank nDCG drop >4 pts on production slice or user complaint rate +1% over baseline.
eva: on mitigation: two immediate experiments — (1) per-channel quant for KV and (2) small calibration sweep using percentile 99.9 vs MLQ; also try per-block scaling (group=32) for the middle layers. these gave partial recovery in offline tests.
maria.g: also worth trying a hybrid model: int4 for feedforward and attention-proj as int8 for middle layers only. costs up a bit vs full int4 but may hit parity. we can try a mixed-precision build.
katie.p: timeline ask from GTN — can we get a recommendation by EOD Monday? they want guidance for next week's enterprise rollout.
maria.g: yes, i'll prepare a short recommendation: default to mixed-fleet with rerank/longform -> int8, short chat -> int4, plus the canary plan and the three mitigation experiments to run during canary.
eil: logging hooks to add: per-request quant-mode tag, rerank_depth, token_count, nDCG, rouge-L, perplexity, and a small sketch of residual norm per layer for debugging.
aj: i'll file a PR to routing to support `X-RW-Flag: rerank` and add token_count-based rule today.
ops-bot: workflow scheduled: `ember18b-int4-canary` starts 2026-04-02T06:00Z, allocation 3%.
maria.g: final operational note — include a human-eval batch (100 rerank cases + 100 longform generation) pre-canary, and add a quick UX smoke where we surface the top-5 rerank outputs to the support team.
katie.p: sounds solid. GTN will want the cost delta table in the recs doc — can you include the modeled 70% and conservative routing numbers?
maria.g: will do. thanks everyone. we'll sync tomorrow after the infra changes. :rocket:
